decision.quote: Thus, the ordering effect reported in Wang and Voss (2015) was identified in this larger, combined sample.
decision.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this request. The full text explicitly distinguishes and empirically retests two separately published findings: (1) the immediate post-regimen paired-associate learning improvement reported in Wang et al. (2014, Science, 10.1126/science.1252900), which is present as shipped row 122, and (2) the multi-week persistence/carry-over ordering effect across the 2-week between-week washout period (comparing Week 2 baseline Pre-Sham performance in the stimulation-first group against Pre-Stim performance in the sham-first group) separately published in Wang and Voss (2015, Hippocampus, 25(8), 877-883, 10.1002/hipo.22416). Although Wang and Voss (2015) analyzed order subgroups from the original crossover experiment, that long-lasting persistence/ordering finding was published in the separate 2015 Hippocampus article rather than the 2014 Science paper, and the current replication explicitly retests and confirms it in Results section 3.1 and Discussion section 4. Note that Luna's identity_quote failed mechanical validation due to line breaks around the author names in the reference list; an intact literal quote from Results section 3.1 is supplied here.

decision.location: Introduction (chunk 8, view_line_1based 10); Study 2a and 2b: Diagnosticity and Grouping (chunk 20, view_line_1based 23); Study 2b Discussion (chunk 30, view_line_1based 32); References (chunk 37, view_line_1based 39)
decision.quote: In Study 2 we attempted to replicate Experiment 4 in Tversky and Gati ( 1978 ) which was reported in Tversky ( 1977 ) as the second study providing support for the diagnosticity effect.
decision.reason: Addressing the prior adjudication and parent_objection explicitly: the source text establishes that Study 2 in Tversky (1977) and Experiment 4 in Tversky and Gati (1978) are two published reports of the exact same original country-similarity diagnosticity experiment (20 sets of 4 countries, N = 33, with diagnosticity effects of 11.8% on choices for b and 11.6% on choices for c), where Tversky (1977) reported the study in summary form and Tversky and Gati (1978) described the same experiment in greater procedural and statistical detail ('Study 2 on the diagnosticity principle, (described in more detail as Experiment 4 in Tversky and Gati, 1978 ) is a conceptual replication using semantic stimuli'). The codebook's 'closest study in the chain' rule applies to replication chains where a finding was subsequently re-tested by others, not to summary versus full companion reports of the same original experiment by the original authors. Under the candidate review report-equivalence rules—which require confirming the absence of the original work/finding across all shipped rows under alternate citations or preliminary/full reports—this underlying original experiment and finding are already represented by shipped row 919 (Tversky, 1977, 10.1037/0033-295x.84.4.327), so Tversky and Gati (1978) is not an independent omitted original. Note also that Luna's identity_quote failed mechanical validation by omitting the space before the closing parenthesis in 'Tversky and Gati, 1978 )'.

decision.location: Abstract; Introduction, Choice of studies for replication; Results, Part 3: convenience-store robbery scenario; References (line 1)
decision.quote: Part 3 is a replication of Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland (1986) with the robbery-scenario – the study that meant to provide the ﬁrst empirical test of norm theory.
decision.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this request. The full text explicitly states and executes a three-part replication across two experiments: Parts 1 and 2 replicate the hitchhiker and car-accident scenarios from Kahneman and Miller (1986, Psychological Review, 93(2), 136-153, 10.1037/0033-295x.93.2.136), which is present as shipped row 1660, whereas Part 3 directly replicates Experiment 1 (the between-subjects convenience-store robbery victim compensation scenario) from Miller and McFarland (1986, 'Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory', Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 12, 513-519). Miller and McFarland (1986) is an independent original empirical paper that is absent from all shipped rows. No DOI is printed in the source text.
